summary: This 3-page report presents a machine-checked Lean 4.35.0 formalization and a zero-floating-point exact-Q certificate verification suite for the locally deterministic polynomial open quantum master equations and critical solutions introduced by Ishizaki and Lee (arXiv:2611.33027 [3]). The standalone Lean module PolyMasterEq.lean proves 18 theorems (zero sorry, zero warnings, zero Classical.choice, zero Lean.ofReduceBool) covering two-qubit characteristic polynomial degrees, critical-parameter factorizations, the exact singularity criterion and odd/even parity obstruction on the critical boundary, and Jaynes-Cummings involution diagonalization plus order-3 Jordan nilpotency at lambda = 2*gamma_0. Complementing the kernel, POLY-MASTER-CERT-1.0 uses Python fractions.Fraction exclusively to replay 16 canonical certificates across four modes in 3.42 ms total while rejecting 60/60 adversarial forgery payloads. All algebraic identities and numerical witnesses printed in the manuscript verify accurately, and the analytic boundaries of the formalization are transparently stated. While the underlying physics and mathematics belong to [3, 5] and the exact Lean theorem signatures and Python code reside in an external repository rather than the PDF, there are no unresolved material objections.
weaknesses: All underlying open-quantum-system results (order-5 master equations, critical factorizations, three-tier singularity/periodicity hierarchy, and Jordan exceptional points) originate from Ishizaki and Lee [3, 5]; the contribution here is strictly formal verification and exact-rational certification.

The formalization covers discrete polynomial-ring (List Int), integer (Z), and small finite matrix (Fin 3, Fin 4) cores plus rational certificates over Q, leaving Laplace-transform contour integration, continuous ODE existence/uniqueness, and formal Z-to-R/C transfer outside the Lean proof boundary.

Because of the compact 3-page format, exact Lean theorem statements (types, quantifiers, hypotheses), verifier schemas, and the 60 adversarial test definitions are not printed in the PDF, preventing independent line-by-line formal audit from the PDF alone without consulting the external repository.

Minor notation and clarity omissions in the prose (e.g., undefined operator T in Sec. 1 item 1, implicit q_- odd hypothesis in Prop. 1.1, and integer vs. reduced-denominator >= 2 JSON encoding in Sec. 3).
